subject: maths
question: A man sold an article at a gain of 39%. If he had sold it for ₹558 more, he would have gained 64%. The cost price (in ₹) of the article is:
solution:
**Given:**

Gain at selling price ₹558 less = 39%

Gain at selling price ₹558 more = 64%

**Formula used:**

Selling Price = Cost Price × (1 + Gain%)

**Calculation:**

Let the Cost Price = ₹x

Selling Price at 39% gain = x × (1 + 39/100) = x × (139/100)

Selling Price at 64% gain = x × (1 + 64/100) = x × (164/100)

Difference in selling prices = ₹558

⇒ x × (164/100) - x × (139/100) = 558

⇒ x × [(164 - 139)/100] = 558

⇒ x × (25/100) = 558

⇒ x = 2232

**∴ The correct answer is option (1).**
